# The Only Health Insurance Stock You Can Own with Michael Ha | The Real Eisman Playbook Episode 51

First listed: 2026-03-23 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

[Back to library](../README.md)

## Source versions

- [YouTube: The Only Health Insurance Stock You Can Own with Michael Ha | The Real Eisman Playbook Episode 51](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jKjg_Ah8DyI) - 2026-03-23
- [Substack: The Only Health Insurance Stock You Can Own with Michael Ha | The Real Eisman Playbook Episode 51](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/the-only-health-insurance-stock-you-d70) - 2026-03-23

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Michael Ha argues that UnitedHealth’s coding exposure and fragmented acquisitions outweigh a simple repricing recovery, while Medicaid may remain difficult until 2027-2029. He favors Alignment’s care model and discusses PBM fee flexibility. Eisman adopts broad sector caution but expressly has not researched Alignment. Subsequent evidence is mixed: UNH segments recovered, Molina remained strained, and Alignment grew while cutting profit guidance. Eisman’s specific expectation that final Medicare Advantage rates would not improve was wrong. Longer Medicaid timing and Alignment’s five-year target remain open, and clinical/coding causality requires more than raw company comparisons.

Full transcript read. Strong focus on segment economics and policy mechanics, but the host political-rate forecast failed and broad caution underweighted the possibility of company-level recovery. Primary results support selective rather than universal conclusions; unverified coding and clinical comparisons remain unresolved.

- [Molina third-quarter 2026 results](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1179929/000117992926000042/moh3q26_er.htm) (2026-10-21): Q3 adjusted EPS $0.89 versus $1.84, nine-month $4.74 versus $13.49; MCR 92.9%. Adjusted full-year guidance at least $5.25. Persistent margin pressure supports slow recovery; management also sees possible Medicaid turning point.
- [UnitedHealth Group third-quarter 2026 results](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/731766/000073176626000255/earningsrelease3q26unh.htm) (2026-10-13): Q3 Optum Health operating earnings $735m versus $41m, margin 3.2% versus 0.2%; adjusted margin 2.6%. Insight earnings $1.279bn versus $920m and Rx $1.718bn versus $1.549bn. Prior periods are recast for Optum Financial. Results show recovery, not uniform segment earnings decline; restructuring and valuation adjustments remain relevant.
- [Alignment Healthcare third-quarter 2026 results](https://ir.alignmenthealth.com/news-releases/news-release-details/alignment-healthcare-reports-third-quarter-2026-results-updates) (2026-10-29): Revenue grew 36.7%, membership 31.2%; adjusted EBITDA fell 32.8% to $21.8m, margin 1.6%, with $8.1m net loss. Medical benefits ratio rose 240bp to 89.5%; full-year profit guidance was reduced despite higher revenue guidance. Nine-month net income still increased, so this is a quarter of pressure, not proven model failure.

## Framework and tools

- Use CMS cohort data to test coding exposure, but control for population composition.
- Separate insurance repricing from provider-service economics.
- Rate-setting lags and selection can move medical costs faster than premiums.
- Vertical ownership does not automatically establish operational integration.
- Compare clinical outcomes on risk-adjusted populations and consistent denominators.
- Map all PBM compensation channels before forecasting profit effects of regulation.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- CMS risk-score cohorts and acquisition timing
- Optum segment margins and recast comparisons
- Medicare Advantage advance and final rate notices
- Medicaid acuity, redeterminations and rate lags
- Medical loss ratios and star ratings
- Hospital admissions per thousand
- PBM formulary, rebate and fee economics

## Source cautions

Michael Ha is the Baird analyst guest. Eisman supplies hypothetical explanations and explicitly adopts overall sector caution/integration critique. Investor repricing counterarguments are exploratory, and Alignment targets belong to Ha alone.
- No opening montage; introduction references prior Claimable and Cuban interviews.
- Life-insurance advertisement at roughly 1110-1205 is excluded from analyst claims.
- ASR repeatedly spells Optum as Optim or Optimum; names normalized.
- Ha corrects 80 hours per week to per month.
- Host adoption is strongest in closing, but ALHC remains the guest recommendation.
- Final CMS policy changed after the interview; distinguish rejected proposed calibration from continuing coding controls.
- Admissions and denial rates are not comparable without denominator and risk-mix controls.
